ingredients.name: water, for boiling the orchid tubers
dried and ground wild orchid tubers, also called chikanda roots
water, for mixing with the groundnuts
hot pepper, chopped, optional for heat

steps.instruction: Bring 2 cups of water to a boil in a pot.
Add 1 cup of dried, ground orchid tubers to the boiling water.
steps.spoken: Add 1 cup of dried, ground orchid tubers, also called chikanda roots, to the boiling water. Boil for about 30 minutes to soften them.

steps.instruction: While the roots boil, toast 1 cup of groundnuts in a dry pan over medium heat.
Stir until the groundnuts are slightly browned and smell toasty.
Let the boiled roots and toasted groundnuts cool to room temperature.
Grind the toasted groundnuts into a fine powder in a blender.
Add 1/2 cup of water to the groundnuts and blend into a smooth paste.
In the same blender, blend 1/2 cup of cooked rice into a smooth paste.
In a large bowl, mix the boiled orchid tubers, groundnut paste and rice paste.
steps.spoken: In a large bowl, mix together the boiled orchid tubers, the groundnut paste and the rice paste. Use your hands or a wooden spoon to combine them thoroughly.

steps.instruction: Add 1 chopped onion, 2 cloves of minced garlic and 1 chopped hot pepper, if using.
Mix in 1 teaspoon of cayenne pepper, 1 teaspoon of ground cumin and salt to taste.
steps.spoken: Mix in 1 teaspoon of ground cayenne pepper, 1 teaspoon of ground cumin and salt to taste. Adjust the seasoning to your preference.

steps.instruction: Roll a handful of the mixture into a sausage shape.
Repeat until all the mixture is used up.
Let the sausages dry and firm up for 3 hours.
steps.spoken: Place the sausages on a clean surface or plate and let them dry and firm up for about 3 to 4 hours.
